title: Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model

nodes.text: ESM3 is a frontier multimodal generative masked language model that reasons jointly over protein sequence, structure, and function, each represented as separate tracks of discrete tokens fused into a single latent space.
nodes.evidence: We present ESM3, a frontier multimodal generative language model that reasons over the sequence, structure, and function of proteins... All three modalities are represented by tokens

nodes.text: ESM3 achieves structural reasoning by encoding 3D atomic structure as discrete tokens via a discrete autoencoder, rather than the complex architecture and 3D-space diffusion used in recent predictive and generative protein models.
nodes.evidence: Structural reasoning is achieved by encoding three-dimensional atomic structure as discrete tokens rather than with the complex architecture and diffusion in three-dimensional space

nodes.text: ESM3 is trained with a generative masked language modeling objective in which the mask is sampled from a noise schedule across all masking rates, differing from classical MLM that uses a single fixed masking rate, enabling generation in any order from any combination of modalities.
nodes.evidence: the supervision is applied across all possible masking rates rather than a single fixed masking rate

nodes.text: An invariant geometric attention mechanism operating in per-residue local reference frames (realized through the same primitives as attention) efficiently processes 3D structure, with optional direct conditioning on atomic coordinates.
nodes.evidence: We propose an invariant geometric attention mechanism to efficiently process three-dimensional structure. The mechanism operates in local reference frames

nodes.text: Tokenization paired with a standard masked language modeling objective and a basic bidirectional transformer is highly effective for both representation learning and generative modeling, despite extensive prior work on specialized protein architectures.
nodes.evidence: we find that tokenization paired with a standard masked language modeling objective and the basic transformer architecture is highly effective for both representation learning and generative modeling

nodes.text: The largest ESM3 (98B parameters) was trained with 1.07e24 FLOPs on 2.78 billion proteins and 771 billion unique tokens; scaling from 1.4B to 98B yields substantial validation-loss improvements across all tracks, greatest in sequence loss.
nodes.evidence: ESM3 at its largest scale was trained with 1.07×1024 FLOPs on 2.78 billion proteins and 771 billion unique tokens, and has 98 billion parameters

nodes.text: ESM3 98B obtains 0.895 mean LDDT on CAMEO single-sequence structure prediction, surpassing ESMFold (0.865 LDDT).
nodes.evidence: ESM3 98B obtains 0.895 mean local distance difference test (LDDT) and surpasses ESMFold (0.865 LDDT)

nodes.text: The structure tokenizer delivers near-perfect reconstruction of protein structure at under 0.3 Angstrom RMSD on CAMEO, enabling atomic-accuracy structure at input and output.
nodes.evidence: This tokenization delivers nearperfect reconstruction of protein structure (<0.3A˚ RMSD on CAMEO

nodes.text: ESM3 generated a novel green fluorescent protein, esmGFP, with only 36% sequence identity to Aequorea victoria GFP and 58% identity to the nearest known fluorescent protein.
nodes.evidence: Our new protein, which we have named esmGFP, has 36% sequence identity to Aequorea victoria GFP, and 58% sequence identity to the most similar known fluorescent protein

nodes.text: Generating a fluorescent protein at 58% identity from known fluorescent proteins is argued to be equivalent to simulating over 500 million years of evolution, since similarly distant natural GFPs are separated by that timescale.
nodes.evidence: the generation of a new fluorescent protein at this distance from existing proteins appears to be equivalent to simulating over 500 million years of evolution

nodes.text: ESM3 can follow out-of-distribution and complex multi-track prompts, generating high-confidence proteins (pTM > 0.8) with under 20% sequence identity and low structural similarity to the training set, including solutions with no matching structure found in nature.
nodes.evidence: ESM3 produces high confidence generations (pTM > 0.8, pLDDT > 0.8) with low sequence and structure similarity to proteins in the training set

nodes.text: Larger ESM3 models are far more responsive to biological alignment and show greater capability to solve the hardest prompts after alignment.
nodes.evidence: Larger models are far more responsive to alignment, and show greater capability to solve the hardest prompts after alignment

nodes.text: ESM3 solves atomic-coordination motif tasks (e.g. serotonin, calcium, protease inhibitor, Mcl-1 binding sites) without retrieving the motif's original scaffold (median TM-score 0.40 to reference), and can compress a serine protease by 33% while maintaining its active site.
nodes.evidence: It does so without retrieving the motif's original scaffold (median TM-score of 0.40 ± 0.10... ESM3 compresses a serine protease by 33% while maintaining the active site structure
